title: Rental Car Insurance in Jordan: CDW, Excess and Deposits Explained
excerpt: Confused by rental car insurance in Jordan? Learn how CDW, excess, deposits and exclusions affect the real cost and risk of your booking.
body:
Rental car insurance is one of the easiest parts of a booking to misunderstand. A price can look simple until you reach the counter and see unfamiliar terms such as CDW, excess, deductible, deposit and excluded damage. The solution is not to buy every option automatically. It is to understand what each layer does before you decide.

## CDW is not the same as zero liability
Collision Damage Waiver, often shortened to CDW, usually limits how much the renter may be responsible for when the rental vehicle is damaged under covered circumstances. It does **not** necessarily mean every type of damage is covered or that your responsibility becomes zero.

Read the exact terms attached to the offer. The remaining amount you may have to pay is often described as an excess or deductible. Different rental companies can apply different amounts and exclusions even when both advertise CDW.

## What is the excess or deductible?
The excess is the amount that can remain your responsibility before or within the provider's protection terms. A lower excess can reduce financial exposure, while a higher excess can come with a cheaper base rate.

This is why the cheapest rental is not always the lowest-risk rental. Compare the full price and the financial responsibility together.

## Deposit versus insurance
A security deposit is not an insurance premium. The provider may place a hold or collect a security amount according to its payment rules. That deposit can be larger than the rental price itself.

Before booking, check:
- Deposit amount
- Accepted card type
- Who must present the card
- When the hold is placed
- How release is handled after return

Do not build your travel budget assuming the deposit is instantly available again the moment you hand back the keys.

## Common exclusions to look for
Insurance terms can contain exclusions for specific damage or behavior. Depending on the provider, items such as tires, wheels, glass, underbody, roof, lost keys, incorrect fuel or unauthorized driving may be treated separately. Off-road use can also violate the rental agreement.

The exact list matters more than the marketing name. Read it before you leave the desk.

## Third-party protection and card benefits
Some travelers have separate rental-car coverage through travel insurance or a credit-card benefit. These products may reimburse eligible costs rather than removing the rental company's deposit or excess at pickup.

If you plan to rely on outside protection, verify the policy before travel. Check country exclusions, vehicle restrictions, maximum rental length and required paperwork. Do not assume a premium card automatically covers every rental in every country.

## What happens after damage?
If an incident occurs, follow the rental company's written instructions. Contact the provider promptly and ask what documentation is required. Depending on the circumstances, official reports or other documents may be necessary for an insurance claim.

Do not promise another party payment or repair terms on the spot without understanding the provider's process. Keep photos, contact details and all paperwork.

## How to compare insurance between offers
When two cars look similar, compare these lines side by side:
- Included protection
- Excess or deductible
- Optional reduction of excess
- Deposit amount
- Excluded damage
- Roadside assistance
- Rules for additional drivers

This comparison often explains why one offer costs more.

## A practical booking strategy
Choose the car first based on your trip, then compare the protection. If you are comfortable with a higher excess and have reliable outside coverage, one option may make sense. If you prefer predictable exposure, paying more for stronger protection may be worth it.

The important point is to decide before the counter, when you have time to read.

## FAQ
### Does CDW mean I cannot be charged for damage?
No. CDW often reduces responsibility but may leave an excess and exclusions. Read the specific rental terms.

### Is the deposit the same as the insurance excess?
No. They are separate concepts. The deposit is a security amount or hold, while the excess describes potential financial responsibility under the protection terms.

### Should I buy extra insurance?
That depends on the included coverage, excess, exclusions and any valid outside protection you already have. Compare them before deciding.

title: What Documents Do You Need to Rent a Car in Jordan?
excerpt: Prepare for a smoother pickup with a clear checklist of the license, passport, payment card and possible International Driving Permit requirements in Jordan.
body:
A rental pickup can take ten minutes or turn into an hour of phone calls depending on whether the documents match the booking. The exact requirements vary by company, but you can avoid most problems by confirming the essentials before you travel.

## Your driving license
Bring the original valid driving license required by the rental company. A photo on your phone is not a reliable substitute for the physical document unless the provider explicitly accepts a digital license.

Some companies require the license to have been held for a minimum period. Others have different rules based on driver age or vehicle class. Check the exact rental conditions rather than relying on a general rule from another company.

## International Driving Permit
An International Driving Permit can be required or requested depending on the rental company, the country that issued your license and the language or script on the original document. It does not replace your national license; where required, it is normally used alongside it.

Enterprise's current Queen Alia Airport rental information, for example, tells international visitors to have an international driving permit when applicable to its requirements. Other providers can apply different wording. Confirm your own booking before travel.

## Passport or identification
International visitors should expect to present a passport or other identification accepted by the rental company. The name should match the booking and license.

If your passport name and card name differ because of transliteration or a recent name change, contact the provider before arrival instead of hoping the counter will resolve it.

## Payment card
Many rentals require a physical payment card in the main driver's name for the rental charge, deposit or both. Debit-card acceptance varies and may come with different conditions.

Check:
- Card type accepted
- Name required on the card
- Available credit for the deposit
- Whether prepaid or virtual cards are accepted

Do not arrive with only a mobile wallet unless the company has explicitly confirmed it can complete the rental that way.

## Additional drivers
Every person who may drive should be declared according to the rental agreement. Additional drivers usually need to present their own qualifying license and identification and may be subject to a fee or age rule.

Letting an unauthorized person drive can create serious problems with the contract and protection if something happens.

## Booking confirmation
Save the booking confirmation offline or take a screenshot. It should show the provider, location, dates, car class and key terms. Airport pickup instructions are especially useful to keep offline in case mobile data is not active when you land.

## Before your flight
Use this checklist:
- Original valid driving license
- International Driving Permit if required
- Passport or accepted ID
- Physical payment card required by the provider
- Booking confirmation
- Provider contact number

If one item is uncertain, ask the rental company in writing before departure.

## Why requirements can differ
Rental companies manage their own risk policies within local legal requirements. That means two providers at the same airport can ask for different documents or apply different age conditions. Search engines can tell you what is common; only the booking terms tell you what your provider will accept.

## FAQ
### Can I rent a car in Jordan with a foreign license?
International travelers commonly rent cars in Jordan, but acceptance depends on the provider, license format and any IDP requirement. Confirm the exact terms.

### Does an IDP replace my home license?
No. An International Driving Permit is generally used together with the original national driving license.

### Can I use a debit card?
Some providers may accept debit cards, while others require a credit card for the deposit. Check the payment rules for the exact offer.

title: Automatic Car Rental in Jordan: What Travelers Should Know
excerpt: Prefer an automatic rental car in Jordan? Learn how to search, compare vehicle classes, confirm transmission and choose the right size for Amman and road trips.
body:
For many international travelers, automatic transmission is not a luxury; it is the difference between a relaxed road trip and learning a new driving skill in unfamiliar traffic. If you want an automatic car in Jordan, search for it deliberately and confirm the transmission before pickup.

## Why automatic can be easier in Jordan
Amman is hilly and can be busy. An automatic car removes clutch work and lets the driver focus more attention on traffic, navigation and road position. It can also reduce fatigue on stop-and-go city driving.

On highways, the difference is less important, but the overall trip may still feel easier if automatic is what you use at home.

## Filter by transmission early
Do not choose a car based on a photo and assume it is automatic. Rental listings often show a model or similar vehicle within a class. Use the transmission filter and read the offer details.

If automatic is essential, confirm it in the booking rather than only mentioning it in a note.

## Economy automatic or larger car?
A small automatic can be ideal for two travelers. It is easier to park in Amman and usually efficient for long road trips. The limitation is luggage space.

For families or groups, compare cargo capacity carefully. A larger sedan or SUV may be more comfortable even when the daily price is higher.

## Automatic does not mean identical performance
Cars in the same rental category can use different engines and transmission designs. A small economy automatic may feel very different on steep Amman roads from a larger vehicle. Drive gently until you understand how the car responds.

Use the parking brake where appropriate and follow the vehicle's own controls rather than assuming every automatic behaves exactly like your car at home.

## Confirm the rental conditions too
Transmission is only one filter. Compare the final price, insurance excess, deposit, mileage and fuel policy. A perfect automatic car with unclear conditions can still be a poor rental.

If you are comparing several automatic offers, use the same dates, pickup location and driver age so the prices are meaningful.

## Airport pickup
Queen Alia Airport is a convenient place to collect an automatic if you plan to drive immediately. Before leaving the lot, adjust the seat and mirrors and find the controls for headlights, wipers and parking brake.

Put your first destination into navigation while parked. Landing, collecting luggage and immediately entering traffic is enough mental load without setting up a phone on the move.

## Road-trip suitability
An automatic economy or sedan can handle the normal paved routes to Petra, the Dead Sea and Aqaba. You do not need an SUV simply because you are traveling through desert landscapes.

Choose an SUV when you need its space or comfort, not as a substitute for checking whether off-road driving is permitted.

## FAQ
### Are automatic rental cars available in Jordan?
Yes, automatic vehicles are widely present in rental searches, but availability depends on dates, location and class.

### Is automatic better for Amman?
Many visitors find it easier because of hills and city traffic, especially if they normally drive automatic at home.

### Should I book a specific model?
Rental companies commonly sell a vehicle class rather than guaranteeing the exact model. Focus on confirmed transmission, size and features that matter to you.

title: SUV Rental in Jordan: When Do You Actually Need One?
excerpt: Thinking about an SUV rental in Jordan? Compare comfort, luggage, family space, fuel and road-trip needs before paying more for a larger vehicle.
body:
SUV rental searches are popular for Jordan because the country is associated with desert landscapes and road trips. But an SUV is not automatically the best car for every itinerary. The main routes between Amman, Petra, the Dead Sea and Aqaba are paved, so the decision should be based on space, comfort and rental terms rather than the landscape in your photos.

## When an SUV makes sense
An SUV can be a strong choice for families, four adults with luggage or travelers who prefer a higher seating position. The extra cargo space can make a long trip easier, especially when everyone has a suitcase.

It can also be more comfortable on long highway days, depending on the model.

## When a smaller car is better
For a couple with two bags, an economy or compact car may be easier in Amman and cheaper to rent and fuel. Larger vehicles can be less convenient in tight parking areas.

Do not pay for space you will not use just because the trip includes Wadi Rum.

## SUV does not equal off-road permission
This is one of the most important distinctions. Renting an SUV does not mean the rental company permits off-road driving. Wadi Rum desert tours are normally handled by local 4x4 vehicles and drivers.

Check the rental agreement before leaving paved roads. Unauthorized use can affect your financial responsibility and protection.

## Five-seat versus seven-seat SUVs
A seven-seat vehicle can look perfect for a group until all seats are raised and the luggage space disappears. If every seat will be occupied, check cargo capacity carefully.

Sometimes two smaller cars or a larger people carrier is more practical than squeezing passengers and bags into a compact seven-seat SUV.

## Fuel and total cost
SUVs can cost more to rent and use more fuel than smaller cars. Compare the total rental price plus likely driving distance, not just the comfort of the vehicle.

If your itinerary includes a full loop through Jordan, a small difference in efficiency can add up.

## Which SUV class?
Rental companies often group several models together. You may book a class rather than a specific vehicle. Focus on confirmed features such as passenger capacity, transmission, luggage estimate and drivetrain if it matters.

If a specific feature is essential, contact the provider rather than assuming the example photo guarantees it.

## FAQ
### Do I need an SUV for Petra?
No. Standard road access to Wadi Musa is paved.

### Do I need an SUV for Wadi Rum?
You need appropriate local 4x4 transport for desert exploration, but your normal rental car typically only needs to reach the arranged meeting area.

### Is an SUV worth it for a family?
Often, yes, when the extra luggage and passenger space materially improves comfort. Compare the total price and cargo layout before booking.

seoDescription: Compare SUV rental in Jordan for families and road trips. Learn when an SUV adds value, when a smaller car is better and why off-road rules matter.

title: 7-Seater Car Rental in Jordan for Families and Groups
excerpt: A seven-seat rental can simplify a Jordan family trip, but seat count is only half the story. Compare luggage space, child seats, drivers and total price.
body:
A seven-seater looks like the obvious answer for a family or group trip in Jordan. Sometimes it is. But the number of seats alone can hide the most important question: where will the luggage go when all seven passengers are inside?

## Count people and bags separately
Before searching, write down the number of adults, children, large suitcases, cabin bags and any stroller or equipment. Then choose a vehicle that handles both passengers and cargo.

Many seven-seat SUVs have limited luggage room when the third row is in use. A people carrier or larger van may be more practical for a full group.

## Child seats
If you need infant, child or booster seats, add them during the booking when available and confirm the provider can supply the correct type. Child seats also use cabin space, so account for them when choosing the class.

Do not assume a child seat is automatically included in a family vehicle.

## One car or two?
For seven adults with heavy luggage, two smaller cars can sometimes be more comfortable than one packed vehicle. The trade-off is two drivers, two fuel bills and potentially two deposits.

Compare the total cost and the group's driving confidence. One vehicle is simpler for navigation and parking together, while two vehicles provide more space.

## Long drives matter
A family road trip may include several hours between Amman and southern Jordan. Legroom, air conditioning and luggage placement become more important after the first hour.

Choose a class that keeps the cabin usable rather than filling every empty space with bags.

## Additional driver
For a longer itinerary, adding a second authorized driver can reduce fatigue. Check the extra-driver fee and make sure the second driver meets the provider's requirements.

Do not allow an undeclared driver to take over simply because the main driver is tired.

## Airport pickup
At Queen Alia Airport, large groups should confirm how the pickup works and whether everyone and all luggage can reach the rental location comfortably. If the company uses a shuttle or off-airport office, understand that process in advance.

## FAQ
### Is a seven-seater enough for seven people and seven suitcases?
Not always. Cargo space can shrink dramatically with all seats in use. Check the vehicle class and luggage capacity.

### Can I add child seats?
Many rental companies offer child-seat extras, subject to availability. Reserve them early and confirm the type you need.

### Is a minivan better than an SUV?
For larger groups with luggage, a people carrier or minivan can offer more usable space than a compact seven-seat SUV.

title: Monthly Car Rental in Amman: When Long-Term Rental Makes Sense
excerpt: Staying in Amman for several weeks? Compare monthly car rental with short-term bookings, including mileage, maintenance, deposit, insurance and flexibility.
body:
Monthly car rental in Amman can make sense for business travelers, extended family visits, temporary residents and anyone who needs a car for several weeks without buying one. The key is to compare a true long-term offer with the cost of simply extending a daily rental.

## Who benefits from monthly rental?
Long-term rental is most useful when you need predictable transport for work, regular trips outside Amman or a multi-week stay. If the car will sit parked most days, other transport may still be cheaper.

Estimate how often you will drive before committing to a full month.

## Compare the monthly total
A lower daily equivalent is attractive, but check what changes with a longer contract. Mileage limits, maintenance responsibility, replacement-car policy and payment schedule can differ from short rentals.

Ask whether the quote is for a calendar month, 30 days or another fixed period.

## Mileage matters more long term
A monthly mileage cap can become important if you commute daily or make frequent trips to Aqaba, Petra or northern Jordan. Calculate your likely distance before choosing an offer.

Unlimited mileage can be valuable, but only if the rest of the terms and price are competitive.

## Maintenance and breakdowns
For a multi-week rental, understand what happens if scheduled maintenance becomes due or the vehicle develops a mechanical issue. The provider should explain where to take the car and whether a replacement is available under the agreement.

Save roadside-assistance details from the first day.

## Deposit and payment
Long-term rentals may involve a substantial deposit or recurring payment structure. Confirm how the card hold works and whether the provider reauthorizes it during the rental period.

Make sure the payment method remains valid for the full contract.

## Choosing the car
For a month, comfort and fuel use matter. A slightly more efficient vehicle can save meaningful money if you drive every day. A compact car is easier in Amman, while a sedan may be more comfortable for frequent highway use.

Do not rent more vehicle than your daily life requires.

## FAQ
### Is monthly car rental cheaper than daily rental?
It can be, because providers may price long-term rentals differently, but compare the full contract and mileage rather than assuming.

### Can I change the car during a monthly rental?
That depends on the provider and contract. Ask about vehicle replacement and maintenance before booking.

### Is monthly rental good for tourists?
It can be for long stays, but travelers spending much of the month in central Amman may not need a car every day.

title: One-Way Car Rental in Jordan: Amman, Aqaba and Airport Returns
excerpt: A one-way rental can save hours of backtracking in Jordan. Learn when different pickup and return locations make sense and which fees to compare.
body:
One-way car rental means collecting a car in one location and returning it somewhere else. In Jordan, that can be especially useful for travelers building a route from Amman to Petra, Wadi Rum and Aqaba without wanting to drive north again solely to return the vehicle.

## When one-way rental is useful
A classic example is pickup at Queen Alia Airport or Amman, then return in Aqaba. The reverse can work for travelers arriving in the south and flying home from Amman.

It can also mean collecting downtown and returning at the airport, which may simplify your final travel day.

## Compare the one-way fee with backtracking
A relocation fee can look expensive until you compare it with extra fuel, hotel nights and several hours of driving. Do the full calculation.

If the fee saves an entire travel day, it may be excellent value. If the locations are close, returning to the original office may still be cheaper.

## Availability varies
Not every vehicle class can be returned to every location. Large vans, premium cars or specialty vehicles may have tighter rules. Search using the exact pickup and return points before building the itinerary around one-way rental.

## Airport returns
If returning at Queen Alia Airport, confirm the exact return area and fuel policy. Do not assume the city office and airport desk are interchangeable.

Leave time for the vehicle handover before your flight.

## Protect your route flexibility
One-way rental is most valuable when it removes unnecessary repetition. It lets your road trip move naturally through Jordan rather than turning around for administrative reasons.

## FAQ
### Can I rent in Amman and return in Aqaba?
Some providers offer this route, subject to availability and a one-way fee.

### Can I return at Queen Alia Airport if I picked up downtown?
Often possible with participating providers, but the airport may be treated as a separate location with its own fee.

### Is one-way rental always more expensive?
The rental may include a relocation charge, but the total trip can still be cheaper after you account for avoided fuel, time and accommodation.

seoDescription: Plan a one-way car rental in Jordan between Amman, Aqaba and Queen Alia Airport. Compare relocation fees with fuel, time and backtracking.

title: Best Car for a Jordan Road Trip: Economy, Sedan or SUV?
excerpt: Choose the right rental car for Jordan by comparing luggage, passenger comfort, fuel, parking and route needs instead of automatically booking the biggest vehicle.
body:
The best car for a Jordan road trip is not one specific model. It is the smallest vehicle that comfortably carries your people and luggage while matching how you plan to drive. An economy car can be perfect for two travelers, while a family may be much happier in a sedan, SUV or people carrier.

## Economy car
Choose an economy car when you are traveling light and want easy parking and lower running costs. It works well on the normal paved routes between Amman, the Dead Sea, Petra and Aqaba.

The limitation is cargo space and long-distance comfort. Two large suitcases can change the equation quickly.

## Compact or midsize sedan
A sedan is the balanced choice for many road trips. It gives more luggage room and highway comfort without the size and fuel use of a large SUV.

For two to four people, this category often provides the best compromise.

## SUV
An SUV makes sense for luggage, family space or a higher seating position. It is not required for the main tourist roads. Do not confuse an SUV booking with permission for off-road use.

If Wadi Rum is on the itinerary, use the local 4x4 arrangements for desert touring rather than treating the rental as a desert vehicle.

## Seven-seater or people carrier
For larger groups, look beyond the passenger number. Seven seats with no cargo room can be less useful than a larger people carrier. Check how many suitcases fit with every seat in use.

## Automatic or manual
Choose the transmission you are comfortable driving. An automatic can reduce workload in Amman's hills and traffic. A manual may be cheaper or more available in some classes, but it is not a good place to learn if you rarely drive one.

## Final decision checklist
Compare passengers, luggage, longest driving day, parking needs, fuel budget and rental price. Then check the insurance, deposit and mileage.

The right car should disappear into the trip. If you spend every day thinking about how cramped, expensive or difficult it is to park, you chose the wrong class.

## FAQ
### Is an economy car enough for Jordan?
Yes for many couples and solo travelers using paved routes. Make sure the luggage fits comfortably.

### Is an SUV safer for a Jordan road trip?
Vehicle safety depends on many factors, not just size. Choose a suitable, well-maintained vehicle and drive according to conditions.

### Do I need four-wheel drive?
Not for the standard paved tourist itinerary. Off-road activities should follow provider rules and local tour arrangements.

title: Petra, Wadi Rum and Aqaba by Car: A 4-Day Southern Jordan Route
excerpt: Connect Petra, Wadi Rum and Aqaba in four days with a rental car while leaving enough time for Petra walking, a desert overnight and the Red Sea.
body:
Petra, Wadi Rum and Aqaba form one of Jordan's strongest short road trips. The distances are manageable, but the experiences are very different: a long day on foot in Petra, a desert excursion in Wadi Rum and a slower Red Sea day in Aqaba. Four days works when you protect those experiences instead of filling every hour with driving.

## Day 1: Arrive in Wadi Musa
Drive to Wadi Musa and stay near Petra. If you are coming from Amman, choose the Desert Highway for speed or the King's Highway when you have the full day for scenery and stops.

Do not try to drive from Amman, tour Petra fully and continue to Wadi Rum in one overloaded day.

## Day 2: Petra
Enter Petra early and dedicate the day to the site. Official opening hours change seasonally, so verify the current schedule before your visit.

After several hours walking, sleep in Wadi Musa again or drive only if you still feel rested and your Wadi Rum arrival is clearly arranged.

## Day 3: Wadi Rum
Drive to the meeting point provided by your Wadi Rum camp or tour operator. Park the rental where instructed and explore the desert using the local 4x4 service.

An overnight gives you sunset and a slower evening without creating another same-day transfer.

## Day 4: Aqaba
Continue to Aqaba for the Red Sea. This is the ideal place to reduce the pace. If you are flying from Amman later, decide whether to return the rental in Aqaba, drive north or extend the trip.

## Car choice
A normal economy car or sedan can cover the paved roads between these destinations. Choose an SUV for space or comfort, not because the itinerary requires off-road capability.

## Rental details that matter
If you collect in Amman and return in Aqaba, price the one-way fee before booking. For a short four-day rental, pickup and return timing also matters because a few hours can affect how the provider calculates the rental period.

## FAQ
### Can I visit Petra and Wadi Rum in one day?
It is possible on a very long itinerary, but a four-day road trip is better when Petra receives its own day and Wadi Rum includes an overnight.

### Do I need a 4x4?
Not for the paved transfers. Use local 4x4 vehicles for desert exploration inside Wadi Rum.

### Can I finish the route in Aqaba?
Yes, and one-way rental can make that efficient if your provider allows a different return location.

title: Dead Sea Day Trip from Amman by Car: Route, Stops and Timing
excerpt: Plan a simple Dead Sea day trip from Amman by rental car, with ideas for Madaba, Mount Nebo, parking, return timing and choosing the right vehicle.
body:
A Dead Sea day trip is one of the easiest ways to make a rental car useful while staying in Amman. The distance is manageable, the road trip can include Madaba or Mount Nebo, and you can control how long you stay rather than following a group-tour timetable.

## Start early enough to keep options open
Leaving Amman in the morning gives you time to add a stop without sacrificing the Dead Sea. You do not need a sunrise departure, but avoid turning the day into a late-afternoon rush.

If your hotel is in a busy part of Amman, allow time to reach the main roads.

## Add Madaba
Madaba fits naturally into a south-west route and can turn a simple swim day into a broader outing. If you also want Mount Nebo, decide in advance how much sightseeing you want before the Dead Sea.

The best road-trip days have two or three priorities, not eight pins.

## Choosing where to access the Dead Sea
Access, parking and facilities vary between hotels, beach clubs and public areas. Decide what experience you want before arriving. A resort day pass can provide showers and changing facilities, while other access points may be simpler.

Check current opening and access conditions directly with the place you plan to use.

## What car do you need?
Any suitable normal rental car can handle the paved route. A compact is easy for a couple; a sedan or SUV may be more comfortable for a family.

The Dead Sea does not require a special off-road vehicle.

## Protect the rental car
After swimming, dry off and keep wet or salty items contained before getting back into the vehicle. Bring a bag for wet clothes and towels.

Do not leave passports, wallets or electronics visible inside the parked car.

## Return to Amman
Plan to drive back before you are exhausted. If you stay for sunset, expect at least part of the return to be after dark and decide whether that fits your comfort level.

A day trip is successful when the final hour does not feel like a race back to the city.

## FAQ
### Can I drive from Amman to the Dead Sea in a rental car?
Yes, the Dead Sea is a common paved-road trip from Amman.

### Can I combine Madaba and the Dead Sea in one day?
Yes, and it is a popular combination when you start with enough time and keep the number of stops reasonable.

### Do I need an SUV?
No. Choose an SUV only if you want the additional passenger or luggage space.

seoDescription: Plan a Dead Sea day trip from Amman by rental car, including Madaba, route timing, vehicle choice, parking considerations and a relaxed return.
